sentence: The problem with the current situation is that, that if you have a sustained period of supply shocks, those can actually start to undermine or to work—to work on de-anchoring inflation expectations.
We continue to discuss whether or not the unemployment rate itself is an adequate measure of how much underutilization of labor resources there really is.

And the maximum level of employment that’s consistent with price stability evolves over time within a—within a business cycle and over a longer period, in part reflecting [the] evolution of the factors that affect labor supply, including those related to the pandemic.

As you said, falling oil prices pull down inflation.

So we do say that risks to the financial system—we say in our longer-run statement of goals and monetary policy strategy that risks to the financial system that could prevent us from achieving our goals are something that we do take into consideration.
We also do see the different measures of slack in the labor market point to different assessments of just what maximum employment is.

By the way, we’re also not at maximum employment, as I mentioned.

I expect that to continue, and I would expect also to see some improvement in the degree of part-time employment that’s for economic reasons.

I think that keeping interest rates low is still appropriate for our economy.

In coming months, as those earlier declines drop out of the calculation, inflation should move up closer to 2 percent and stabilize around that level over the medium term.
It would consist of inflation plus—plus productivity growth.

And, as I think all of us—having that expectation and that if the economy continued to progress along the lines that we expected and we continued to see the risks as balanced—do regard it as appropriate to gradually remove accommodation that’s in place by having several interest rate increases this year.
So, as I mentioned, we’re going to be looking at all of those things: activity, labor market, inflation.
Everyone, particularly people on fixed incomes, and at the lower part of the income distribution are better off with stable prices.
